```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5)
```

```{r}
library(pgmcompR)
```

We pretend not to know the chest clinic ("Asia") network of Lauritzen and
Spiegelhalter (1988) and learn it from simulated patient records.

```{r}
truth <- example_network("asia")
records <- simulate_bn(truth, 5000, seed = 2024)
head(records)
```

## Parameters for a known structure

With the structure fixed, `fit_parameters()` estimates the CPDs. Maximum
likelihood uses relative frequencies; Bayesian estimation uses the posterior
mean under a Dirichlet prior, which is also the posterior predictive
probability of the next patient.

```{r}
skeleton_bn <- bayesian_network(edges(truth))
mle <- fit_parameters(skeleton_bn, records, method = "mle")
bayes <- fit_parameters(skeleton_bn, records, method = "bayes",
                        prior = "bdeu", equivalent_sample_size = 10)
get_cpd(mle, "tub")
get_cpd(bayes, "tub")
```

`tub` given `asia = "yes"` rests on few records (about 1% of patients visited
Asia), and the prior visibly shrinks it. Rare parent configurations are where
the choice of estimator matters.

### Unobserved parent configurations

If a parent configuration never occurs, maximum likelihood is undefined.
pgmcompR never fills such columns silently: the `unobserved` argument decides.

```{r, error = TRUE}
few <- records[1:30, ]
fit_parameters(skeleton_bn, few, unobserved = "error")
```

```{r}
fit_uniform <- fit_parameters(skeleton_bn, few, unobserved = "uniform")
```

### Structural zeros

Some cells are impossible by definition: `either` is the logical OR of
`tub` and `lung`. Structural zeros keep them at zero even under a prior.

```{r}
zeros <- matrix(c(FALSE, TRUE,  TRUE, FALSE,  TRUE, FALSE,  TRUE, FALSE), 2)
fz <- fit_parameters(skeleton_bn, records, method = "bayes",
                     structural_zeros = list(either = zeros))
get_cpd(fz, "either")
```

### Missing values and EM

Real records are incomplete. Suppose smoking status is missing for a fifth
of patients:

```{r}
set.seed(3)
incomplete <- records
incomplete$smoke[sample(nrow(incomplete), 1000)] <- NA
em <- fit_parameters(skeleton_bn, incomplete, method = "em", max_iter = 50, seed = 1)
attr(em, "iterations")
round(diff(attr(em, "loglik")), 4)[1:5]
get_cpd(em, "smoke")
```

The log likelihood increases monotonically, as EM guarantees. The expected
counts in each E step are computed exactly with a junction tree per
distinct missingness pattern.

## Learning the structure

### Conditional independence tests

```{r}
ci_test(records, "smoke", "dysp")
ci_test(records, "lung", "bronc", "smoke")
```

### Constraint based: PC

```{r}
pc_graph <- pc_algorithm(records, alpha = 0.01)
pc_graph
```

The PC algorithm returns a partially directed graph. Undirected edges are
not oriented by the data: every DAG in the Markov equivalence class
explains the observations equally well. The deterministic node `either`
violates the faithfulness assumption that PC relies on, which explains the
missing `either -- xray` edge.

### Score based: hill climbing, tabu search and MMHC

```{r}
hc <- hill_climb(records, score = "bic")
tabu <- tabu_search(records, score = "bic")
mm <- mmhc(records, score = "bic")
compare_graphs(truth, hc)
compare_graphs(truth, tabu)
compare_graphs(truth, mm)
c(hc = attr(hc, "score"), tabu = attr(tabu, "score"), truth = network_score(truth, records, "bic"))
```

Arc reversals inside an equivalence class do not change BIC or BDeu, so
"misoriented" arcs are expected; compare equivalence classes instead:

```{r}
markov_equivalent(tabu, truth)
```

### Prior knowledge

Blacklists forbid arcs, whitelists require them, and tiers forbid arcs from
later to earlier groups. A visit to Asia and smoking precede the diseases,
which precede the symptoms and the X-ray:

```{r}
tiers <- list(c("asia", "smoke"), c("tub", "lung", "bronc", "either"), c("xray", "dysp"))
hc_tiers <- hill_climb(records, tiers = tiers)
compare_graphs(truth, hc_tiers)
```

### Edge stability

The bootstrap shows which edges the data support firmly:

```{r}
strength <- bootstrap_structure(records[1:1500, ], R = 20, algorithm = "hill_climb", seed = 1)
head(strength[order(-strength$strength), ], 10)
averaged_network(strength, threshold = 0.7)
```

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)}
plot(averaged_network(strength, 0.5), edge_strength = strength)
```

## A caution

Observational structure learning recovers at best a Markov equivalence
class, under assumptions (faithfulness, no hidden confounders, correct
tests). A learned arrow is not, by itself, evidence of a causal effect.
